work.projectDescription:
I will create a new solo Unity exploration and puzzle game from scratch. The player will explore a small outpost, discover clues, solve an environmental puzzle, and activate a beacon to complete the mission.
I will create new scenes, scripts, and project assets for this Final rather than reuse my previous coursework. I will be responsible for planning, programming, level design, testing, documentation, version control, and delivery. Any AI assistance or external resources used will be documented.
work.engine: Unity 6 / C# / Visual Studio Code / Git and GitHub
work.gitEvidence: I first edited README.md in VS Code, committed and pushed it, and verified that the updated text appeared on GitHub, commit e923ce1. I then reused my Week12B Explorer Beacon project to test Unity. I changed the Main Camera field of view to 65 outside Play Mode, saved the scene, and tested beacon activation. I pushed ToolTest in commit e9376eb, downloaded the repository from GitHub, and opened the downloaded project in Unity. The field of view remained 65, and beacon activation displayed “Communication restored.” This reused project is preparation evidence, not newly earned Final scope.
work.aiVerify: I will inspect and explain suggested code, run it in Unity, test normal and boundary cases, compare expected and actual results, and check official documentation. I will record failures, fixes, and AI assistance.
work.notes: I can open and test Unity scenes, change and save Inspector settings, and commit and push files using VS Code and GitHub. For example, I changed the camera field of view to 65 and verified that the downloaded project retained the change and beacon activation worked. I can record test results and organize evidence. AI assisted with the earlier project’s source, models, documentation, and today’s instructions. I still need practice explaining and modifying C# scripts independently and defining a realistic Final scope.
work.role: Solo developer — planning, implementation, testing, documentation, version control, and release.

requirements.title: Working project foundation
requirements.evidence: Working source and build (60); authored program logic (35); meaningful tests (20); run guide and evidence map (20); individual explanation (15).

requirements.title: Save and restore progress
requirements.evidence: Save meaningful state; close and reopen the program; demonstrate correct restoration and invalid-file handling.

requirements.title: Branching story or mission state
requirements.evidence: Demonstrate at least two meaningful outcomes, their conditions and a state-transition test.

requirements.title: Settings that persist
requirements.evidence: Provide useful settings, validate changes, save them and demonstrate restoration. This must extend beyond the same progress data.

requirements.title: Inventory or structured collection
requirements.evidence: Add, remove and inspect structured items. Test limits and invalid actions.

requirements.title: Reusable dialogue or interaction system
requirements.evidence: Use data-driven interactions in more than one situation; show how new content can be added.

requirements.title: Accessible controls and interface
requirements.evidence: Demonstrate keyboard access, readable contrast, clear feedback and one user-tested accessibility improvement.

requirements.title: Modular architecture
requirements.evidence: Show a module/class diagram, clear responsibilities and a change made without rewriting unrelated systems.

requirements.title: Automated regression tests
requirements.evidence: Run meaningful normal, boundary and failure tests. Show a defect the suite detects.

requirements.title: External playtest and revision
requirements.evidence: Use consented feedback from at least three testers; document problems, fixes and retest evidence.

requirements.title: Measure and improve performance
requirements.evidence: Record a repeatable baseline, identify a measured bottleneck, improve it and compare results.

requirements.title: Repeatable build and release pipeline
requirements.evidence: Demonstrate a reproducible build, checks, artifact/version naming and rollback or recovery notes.

requirements.title: Secure input and data handling
requirements.evidence: Document threats relevant to the project and test validation, safe error handling and protection of private data.

requirements.title: Public release on an approved platform
requirements.evidence: Publish an accessible working build, versioned release notes and installation/run instructions on Steam or an approved equivalent. Platform acceptance alone earns no points.

requirements.title: Front-facing HTML product page
requirements.evidence: Create an original responsive product page with screenshots, accurate features, credits, accessibility and a working release/download link.

requirements.title: Architecture defense and maintenance guide
requirements.evidence: Individually explain unfamiliar code sections, trace data flow and make a small requested change.
